Scope note: respond_to_interest implements the CURRENT-reply semantics (match the Interest keyexpr against held tokens, tag each reply with the inbound interest_id, terminate with a DeclFinal). A FUTURE-only interest (remember the interest and reply to tokens declared LATER) is not separately tracked — the proactive declare covers the FUTURE path for peers already subscribed when a token is declared; a dedicated future-interest table is a possible refinement only if a future-only foreign consumer ever needs it (z_get_liveliness is CURRENT-only; z_sub_liveliness uses CURRENT for replay + FUTURE for the proactive stream, both covered).

changes_bullets: wz-switchboard-codegen: new `owned_field_move(sce_type, expr)` threads `.into()` for a scalar string/bytes schema field. SCE decodes a scalar string/bytes codec field as a borrowed view (`&'a str` / `&'a [u8]`, lifetime tied to the wire buffer) but the native-lowered `<Machine><Variant>Payload` struct holds it owned (`String` / `Vec<u8>`, no lifetime -- it derives Clone+Default and outlives the buffer once queued). `.into()` bridges the two with the target inferred from the struct field's known type, so no alloc/std path is named and the one shared helper compiles on both the AP (std) and MCU (no_std+alloc) tiers. Under `reassembly` a per-(slot,channel) Router (mcu_reassembly = ReassemblyDispatcher<4,4096>, the same run_session owns) is built before the loop; the FrameOutOfOrder arm aborts the channel's in-progress chain (reasm.abort_channel via peer_index_by_src), the Fragment arm parses the inbound T_MID_FRAGMENT (parse_inbound -> InboundFrame::Fragment) and reassembles via ingest_multicast_fragment (per-peer SN gate -> chain -> the completed message fans as the SAME FramePayload Poll a whole Frame does), and the Close arm aborts the departing peer's chains before close_by_src. The sweep arm becomes sweep_with(now, abort_peer_chains) + sweep_reporting under `reassembly`, the bare sweep otherwise. Without the feature the arms keep the prior drop-Fragment behaviour (pico fragmentation-off).

crates/wz-session-lwip/Cargo.toml: a new `transport-fragmentation` feature = [reassembly, wz-session-core/transport-fragmentation] forwards the core umbrella (reassembly + codec-fragment + alloc) and re-uses this crate's reassembly forward for the wz-runtime-lwip Router. No drive-loop code change for TX: run_multicast_session already frames its next_tx seam through the shared multicast_tx_emit SSOT, which splits an oversize payload via multicast_frame_or_fragments once the feature is on - exactly as the AP loop. The MCU TX port was a feature forward; the fragmentation SSOT was already shared (R311ko).

Test run_multicast_session_reassembles_a_fragmented_put_over_loopback (gated transport-fragmentation,codec-push): the real-lwIP fragment leg. A 200-byte z_put at batch_size 64 is proven to fragment (>1 datagram via a direct multicast_tx_emit probe), multicast to the group, echoed back, and reassembled by the Fragment RX arm into one observed Push (no ReassemblyDropped). The pre-admitted peer JOIN advertises batch_size 64 to match self: validate_join admits only when the JOIN's batch_size equals the receiver's params, else the echoed fragments hit an UnknownPeer drop.

CORRECTION from the review's CRITICAL finding: the collapse also re-aligned the interceptor ORDER. The old demo/test call order was ACL -> downsampling; the new fixed order is downsampling -> ACL (zenoh's). Because InterceptorChain::admit short-circuits (Iterator::all) and the downsampler records its rate timer only on the messages IT admits (downsampling.rs:92), the order is OBSERVABLE when an ACL selectively denies: in zenoh order the downsampler stamps a message the ACL then denies (consuming the rule's rate budget); in the old order an ACL-denied message short-circuited before the downsampler saw it. So this is behavior-ALIGNED-to-zenoh, not behavior-preserving — zenoh's downsampler likewise stamps a message its ACL later denies (zenoh downsampling.rs:242-244 updates the timestamp only on admit, and the factory runs downsampling before the ACL).

changes_bullets: (HIGH) issue_and_collect now wraps the on_final await in a tokio::time::timeout backstop (ALIGNER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS + ALIGNER_BACKSTOP_SLACK_MS) so a spawned alignment task is SELF-BOUNDED. The prior ALIGNER_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS doc claimed the wire with_timeout_ms guarantees on_final fires when a replica is unreachable, but the reply-timeout sweep (ReplyRegistry::sweep_timed_out) is a SEPARATE task -- R268 relocated it OUT of drive_session_until_terminal -- so a session without an app-spawned sweep would hang final_rx.await forever on a silent peer, leaking the detached task + its Arc<Mutex<StorageState>> clone per divergence. The backstop resolves regardless; the doc is corrected to state this honestly.

(MEDIUM) digest_keyexpr_zid_hex now requires the zid chunk to be all ascii-hexdigit (exactly what zid_to_zenoh_hex emits, so a legit peer never fails) -- defense-in-depth: a crafted/non-conformant peer keyexpr like @-digest/a$*/<fp> would otherwise splice a keyexpr WILDCARD into the aligner query keyexpr (aligner_keyexpr_for_hex), fanning a targeted Diff pull (and this replica's DigestDiff) out to many replicas. +3 rejection asserts.

(MEDIUM) run_alignment now truncates a Discovery query's replies to the first (replies.truncate(1)): zenoh defensively stops after the FIRST Discovery reply (core.rs:567-572) because Monotonic may still deliver several; without the guard several Discovery replies fanned into several All pulls.

(LOW) run_alignment now bounds the followup queue with MAX_ALIGNMENT_QUERIES (100k). A conformant peer's refinement tree stays far below; a hostile peer answering ANY query with fresh Discovery replies can no longer grow the queue unbounded (zenoh has the same exposure via unbounded task spawns; wz's single-task drain makes a cheap cap natural). Hitting it abandons THIS pass -- the next digest tick re-triggers if still diverged, so a deep alignment still converges over ticks.
